scenes.narration: Merge sort treats every single value as a sorted run. It merges neighbouring runs of width 1 into pairs, then pairs into fours, and so on, until one run holds everything.
scenes.caption: Merge small sorted runs into bigger ones

scenes.narration: The first two runs, 5 and 1, merge into the sorted pair 1, 5.
scenes.caption: merge 5 | 1

scenes.narration: Then 8 and 3 become 3, 8. Every run now has width 2.
scenes.caption: merge 8 | 3

scenes.narration: Now we merge runs of width 2. Taking the smaller front value each time, 1, 5 and 2, 4 become 1, 2, 4, 5. The run 3, 8 has no partner yet, so it waits.
scenes.caption: merge 1 5 | 2 4

scenes.narration: Last, the run of 4 merges with 3, 8. The array is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8.
scenes.caption: merge 1 2 4 5 | 3 8

scenes.narration: Merging only ever compares the front values of two sorted runs, so each round is one quick pass, and there are about log n rounds.
scenes.caption: Summary
points: Every merge takes two sorted runs
O(n log n) every time, with O(n) extra space

quiz.question: Merge sort performs two merges on 4, 3, 2, 1. What is the array afterwards?
quiz.explanation: The pairs 4, 3 and 2, 1 each become sorted.

quiz.question: Merge sort performs three merges on 4, 3, 2, 1. What was the run width of the third merge?
quiz.explanation: The third merge joins two runs of width 2 into the final run.
